prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: full-fidelity desktop web app direction comp, 1440x900 landscape
Primary request: Design the first viewport of Bork, a polished dog-themed short-post social app and resume project, as a tactile creator-hardware desk instrument called Fetch Console. The app must visibly function as a readable social feed, not as a product photograph or synth dashboard.
Scene/backdrop: one gunmetal chassis filling the browser viewport, with bone and putty keycap controls in a compact rail, one broad amber live-feed screen, one safety-orange publish key, and minimal knurled detail.
Subject: Bork dog social feed. Show logo/name Bork, navigation labels Feed, My kennel, Settings; a composer labeled “Leave a bork”; authentic short dog posts with warm dog portraits, timestamps and names. Use truthful demo copy only, no metrics or customer claims.
Style/medium: high-end product UI mockup with tactile industrial controls and serious typographic discipline, distinctly not Twitter.
Composition/framing: 1440x900 straight-on browser viewport. The broad amber feed screen dominates. Navigation keys group in one row/rail. The single orange BORK key is the obvious primary action. No control duplicates a normal text affordance.
Lighting/mood: controlled studio-soft interface light, precise and satisfying rather than sci-fi.
Color palette: #242926 gunmetal, #ddd4bd bone, #f0642f safety orange, #d89b3b amber status, near-black legends.
Materials/textures: restrained gunmetal, dye-sublimated keycaps, amber status glass, shallow layered key shadows, one knurled edge.
Text (verbatim where legible): “Bork”, “LIVE FEED”, “Leave a bork”, “BORK”, “Feed”, “My kennel”, “Settings”, “Mabel”, “Found the sunny square. Claimed it.”
Constraints: desktop web interface; familiar posting and reading affordances; dog-first and self-aware; no fake traction; no bone-shaped buttons; no paw-print wallpaper; no gradients; no glassmorphism; no excessive knobs; no Twitter blue; no three-column Twitter clone.
Avoid: photograph of physical hardware, audio workstation, dashboard metrics, sci-fi HUD, novelty controls, illegible tiny labels, extra features.
